source_node.label: Exploit Raspberry Pi Default Credentials (CVE-2021-37594 / Standard Config)
source_node.precondition: Target Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS <= 5.10 is reachable over SSH or local network, and default 'pi:raspberry' credentials have not been changed.
source_node.postcondition: Attacker obtains authenticated shell access as user 'pi' with sudo privileges on Raspberry Pi OS.

target_node.label: RaspAP Unrestricted Web Console Command Execution
target_node.precondition: Authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5 web interface running on the Raspberry Pi OS target.
target_node.postcondition: Remote arbitrary shell command execution, file upload, and persistent OS-level code execution on the underlying Raspberry Pi.

source_evidence.description: An issue was discovered in includes/webconsole.php in RaspAP 2.5. With authenticated access, an attacker can use a misconfigured (and virtually unrestricted) web console to attack the underlying OS (Raspberry Pi) running this software, and execute commands on the system (including ones for uploading of files and execution of code).

target_node.label: piSignage Arbitrary File Download via Path Traversal
target_node.precondition: Network access to piSignage web application (< 2.6.4) and possession of low-privilege authenticated user credentials on the service.
target_node.postcondition: Arbitrary file disclosure on the Raspberry Pi host via 'api/settings/log?file=../' parameter, exposing configuration data, source code, and credentials.

source_evidence.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.

source_node.label: Oculus Browser Remote UI HTML Injection and Potential Code Execution
source_node.precondition: User visits an attacker-controlled remote web page using Oculus Browser versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11.
source_node.postcondition: Injection of arbitrary HTML into the Oculus Browser UI, enabling UI spoofing and arbitrary code execution in the context of the browser process.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hard Link Arbitrary File Write Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Local low-privilege execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop < 1.44.0.32849, where OVRRedir.exe runs as a privileged process.
target_node.postcondition: Privileged arbitrary file write via hard link redirection to log files, resulting in local privilege escalation to SYSTEM/Administrator.

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher.exe Process Handle Leak Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Local low-privilege process execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop > 1.39 and < 31.1.0.67.507.
target_node.postcondition: Acquisition of a leaked privileged process handle from OVRServiceLauncher.exe, leading to local privilege escalation.

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Due to a bug with management of handles in OVRServiceLauncher.exe, an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.
